key_insight: FSG-RL trains a math-reasoning model with function-structured graphs plus executable verifiers, improving not just code execution but mathematical correctness.
engineering_relevance: The method suggests a practical RL pipeline for solver systems that need intermediate verification, credit assignment, and structured memory rather than relying only on final-answer rewards.
method: SFT learns to map function graphs to Python implementations.
GRPO uses answer-gated rewards with span-level credit assignment.
Teacher supervision and structured memory can be added during continued RL.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark built from GSM8K, MathQA, MATH, and Omni-MATH, GRPO improved final-answer accuracy from 43.25% to 67.50% and full solution success from 32.25% to 52.25% under a unified evaluation protocol.
watch_item: Executable outputs can still be mathematically wrong, so verifier design and private specification quality are critical implementation risks.
paper_title: Function-Structured Reinforcement Learning with Executable Verifiers for Mathematical Reasoning
